STANDING RULE adopted from the T-034/T-032 pg_net defect (evaluator recommendation, confirmed by the orchestrator's migration audit): any SECURITY DEFINER function that invokes an EXTENSION function must have an integration test that EXECUTES it, not merely inspects prosrc/pg_proc source text. The escaped defect - invoke_cron_endpoint calling http_get in the `extensions` schema where pg_net installs its functions in `net` - would have failed every deployed cron silently and passed THREE review layers (implementation, evaluation, orchestrator snapshot review) precisely because every assertion inspected the artifact rather than resolving/running the function. Audit result recorded: grep of supabase/migrations for extensions.http_ found the defect ONLY in the two migrations already handled under T-034; the original T-032 migration (20260720000000:100) still literally contains `perform extensions.http_get(`, left as-is because T-034 fixed it forward with CREATE OR REPLACE and this repo does not edit applied migrations - on a clean apply the broken function is created then replaced before job_cron_config is ever populated, so the transient broken state is unreachable and db:validate confirms convergence. T-042's deployment doc should state this fix-forward history so a future reader of the original migration is not misled.

findings.summary: V-003 built-bundle scan is not wired as a standalone CI artifact. The SPA-source guard src/ui/src/auth/browserClientBoundary.test.ts proves the SPA never imports the server config module or the service-role key, but the deployment-time scan of the built src/ui/dist (for the server variable NAMES SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/DATABASE_URL/DIRECT_DATABASE_URL/CRON_SECRET/INTERNAL_JOB_SECRET and src/server path fragments) required by AC-002/V-003 does not yet exist in scripts/. Per the T-042 brief this was to be verified-or-noted, not built by this docs/config task; documented as such in docs/environment-variables.md. Recommend a follow-up task (or fold into T-018) to add scripts/ci/scan-bundle.ts run after npm run build:ui.

V-114 repo-wide secret-hygiene scan script is not wired. The two example files are guarded by src/server/tests/integration/env-examples.test.ts (rejects JWT-shaped strings and inline-credential postgres URLs), and .gitignore covers .env*/.vercel/logs, but there is no CI-safe script scanning all tracked files for committed secrets. Noted rather than built (docs/config task). Recommend a follow-up scripts/ci/scan-secrets.ts.
